In RAN1#119 meeting, the following conclusion and agreements were made for the issue of inter-vendor training collaboration and data collection [1]. In this contribution, we continue to share our views on inter-vendor training collaboration based on [2]. In RAN1#118 meeting, to study the performance impact resulting from non-ideal UCI feedback (such as UL transmission error, UCI drop/omission), RAN1 made one relevant agreement as shown below [3], which defines three scenarios (Scenario A/B/C) and the UCI loss modelling for Case 2. In this section, we provide evaluation results based on the agreement. In Case 2, the past CSI information is used at both UE side and NW-side to compress/reconstruct the CSI of current time instance. The measured CSI needs to be fed into UE-sided AI encoder and the feedback CSI needs to be fed into NW-sided AI decoder for updating past CSI information, as shown in Figure 1. Since there is high correlation over the temporal domain in the scenario of low UE speed, the compression rate or the reconstruction accuracy could be improved by using past CSI information at both sides. However, this improvement is achieved based on the assumption of ideal UCI feedback. If non-ideal UCI feedback is considered, it is unclear how much gain could be achieved, and what kind of mitigation method could be used to reduce the performance loss resulting from UCI loss. Figure 1: Non-ideal UCI feedback for Case 2. Basically, there are at least two reasons leading to non-ideal UCI feedback or UCI loss: UL transmission error, CSI drop/omission based on the CSI report principle. Once UCI loss happens due to the above reasons, NW side may have no feedback CSI to be fed into NW-sided AI decoder for updating NW-sided past CSI information. Since UE side updates its past CSI information regardless of whether UCI loss happens or not, there would be mismatch between UE-sided and NW-sided past CSI information. Such kind of mismatch may lead to the performance loss for Case 2. If the performance loss is not negligible, some method must be considered to mitigate the impact. Figure 2 illustrates Scenario A/B/C and corresponding mitigation methods if UCI loss happens. For Scenario B, two mitigation methods are considered in this contribution, M1: Default values (such as zeros) as feedback CSI are fed into NW-sided AI decoder for updating past CSI information. M2: NW-sided past CSI information is reset as historical values. For Scenario B/C, since UCI loss is known at NW side or both sides, the past CSI information is reset as historical values at NW side or both sides. This figure only shows that the past CSI information is reset as historical values of last time instance. When UCI loss happens for several consecutive time instances, the past CSI information may be reset as historical values of several time instances before, i.e., the latest available historical CSI. Figure 2: The illustration of Scenario A/B/C and corresponding mitigation method. Simulation was performed to evaluate the SGCS performance with Scenario A/B/C and different mitigation methods, as shown in Table 1. The simulation assumption is given in the appendix and UCI loss rate is set as 10%. It can be observed that compared with Scenario A, the performance loss could be significantly reduced in Scenario B and Scenario C with a proper mitigation method. Table 1: SGCS performance impacts resulting from non-ideal UCI feedback. Based on this evaluation result, we have the following observation. Observation 1: For Case 2 (AI/ML-based CSI compression assisted by past CSI information), compared with Scenario A (without UCI loss), The performance loss of 7.6% is observed in Scenario B (UCI loss is only known at NW side) if default values (all-zeros) are fed into CSI recons

However, this improvement is achieved based on the assumption of ideal UCI feedback. If non-ideal UCI feedback is considered, it is unclear how much gain could be achieved, and what kind of mitigation method could be used to reduce the performance loss resulting from UCI loss. Figure 1: Non-ideal UCI feedback for Case 2. Basically, there are at least two reasons leading to non-ideal UCI feedback or UCI loss: UL transmission error, CSI drop/omission based on the CSI report principle. Once UCI loss happens due to the above reasons, NW side may have no feedback CSI to be fed into NW-sided AI decoder for updating NW-sided past CSI information. Since UE side updates its past CSI information regardless of whether UCI loss happens or not, there would be mismatch between UE-sided and NW-sided past CSI information. Such kind of mismatch may lead to the performance loss for Case 2. If the performance loss is not negligible, some method must be considered to mitigate the impact. S beamforming is transparent to UE. In solution 2, from FL perspective, the UE processing is not clear. According to Apple’s comment in the last meeting, a simple implementation is that UE should exclude a layer from the target CSI if the layer has an SGCS with the restricted DFT beam(s) higher than the SGCS threshold. But the algorithm seems to be lack of optimization as UE may have to drop all layers. Whether the DFT bases is over-sampled or not, how many oversampling group can be restricted, how many beams / bases can be restricted E.g., if oversampling is supported in solution 1, UE may use the unrestricted oversampling group to do the projection, so the final target CSI to be fed into the encoder is the same as the target CSI without CBSR. What is the metric used for restriction, hard restriction or soft restriction. Model generalization performance, e.g., training from dataset without CBSR, but test in a dataset with CBSR, or vice versa. With above, let us consider following proposal as a starting point for discussion. Proposal 4.1 (medium): CBSR Study the feasibility of following solutions to facilitate restricting the reported CSI in a certain beam direction: Solution 1: Representing precoding matrix W=W1*W2 or W=W1*W2*Wf, and apply restrictions on the DFT bases in W1. Solution 2: The SGCS between the reported precoding matrix W and a set of restricted DFT bases should not exceed a configured SGCS threshold. Solution 3: The beam restriction is absorbed into the CSI-RS beamforming The study includes following aspects: Whether the DFT bases is over-sampled or not, how many oversampling group can be restricted, how many beams / bases can be restricted What is the metric used for restriction, hard restriction or soft restriction. Associated UE behaviour and complexity Model generalization performance, e.g., training from dataset without CBSR, but test in a dataset with CBSR, or vice versa.

Solution 2: The SGCS between the reported precoding matrix W and a set of restricted DFT bases should not exceed a configured SGCS threshold. Solution 3: The beam restriction is absorbed into the CSI-RS beamforming The study includes following aspects: Whether the DFT bases is over-sampled or not, how many oversampling group can be restricted, how many beams / bases can be restricted What is the metric used for restriction, hard restriction or soft restriction. Associated UE behaviour and complexity Model generalization performance, e.g., training from dataset without CBSR, but test in a dataset with CBSR, or vice versa.

Mod’s suggestion: A proposal is suggested for functionality-based LCM framework for further discussion. Related proposals in tdocs Intel: Proposal 5 LG: Proposal 12 OPPO: Proposal 16 CAICT: Proposal 5 CATT: Proposal 13 CMCC: Proposal 14 Xiaomi: Proposal 10 DCM: Proposal 13 Samsung: Proposal 16 Nokia: Proposal 5, 6 RS resource configuration for performance monitoring At least, 5 companies (e.g., IDC, vivo, Sony, Nokia, QC) are discussing the configurations of RS resource, but some of the proposals are generic and lack details Mod’s assessment: The detailed configurations/signaling seems more suitable for WI.
